paper.title: Adaptive Bandit Algorithms for Contextual Matching Markets

Arms have fixed, strict, known preferences over players

Each player has its own unknown parameter theta_i; contexts of each arm drawn i.i.d. from an arm-specific distribution

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual matching markets with adversarial contexts
unmapped: Two-sided matching market with known arm preferences over players
Regret is the alpha-approximate Delta-optimal stable regret: exact player-optimal stable share when delta_min(t) > Delta, alpha times epsilon-optimal stable share otherwise
Access to an offline (alpha, gamma, eps)-approximation oracle for stable matching
settings.definition_quote: we now analyze worst-case scenarios in which no assumptions are placed on context generation, i.e., contexts may even be chosen by an adaptive adversary. ... $Reg_i^{\alpha, \Delta}(T) = \sum_{t = 1}^T [\mU_i^*(t) \ind{\delta_{\min}(t) > \Delta} + \alpha \mU^{\varepsilon}_{i}(t) \ind{\delta_{\min}(t) \leq \Delta}] - \mathbb{E} [\sum_{t = 1}^T y_i(t)]$

symbols.Delta_pref: paper's minimum preference gap: sup{Delta : P(delta_min >= Delta) >= 1 - log T/(T Delta^2)}

tuning: eta = R sqrt(d log((1+T B_x^2/lambda)/delta)) + lambda^{1/2} B_theta

source.label: thm:stochastic_context_upper_bound
source.quote: Assume that the environment follows Assumption 1, 2 and 3, and the contexts are stochastic. Following the BARB algorithm, the player-optimal stable regret for $p_i \in \gN$ is $Reg_i(T) = \gO (\frac{\log^2 T}{\Delta_{\min}^2} + \frac{\log T}{\Delta_{\min}^2}) = \gO (\frac{\log^2 T}{\Delta_{\min}^2})$.

results.notes: Per-player regret against player-optimal stable matching; defined through expected utilities, hence pseudo-regret. Hidden dependence on N, d in constants (proof: 64 B_y (eta^2 N d log(...)/Delta^2 + ...)). Delta_min here is the paper's probabilistic gap, not the canonical smallest arm gap.

symbols.lambda_tilde: lower bound on the minimum eigenvalue of the context covariance matrix (Assumption 4)

conditions: Assumptions 1-3 (bounded contexts, conditionally subgaussian noise, bounded theta)
tuning: initial exploration length T_1, doubled across batches

source.label: thm:betc_upper_bound
source.quote: Assume that the environment follows Assumption 1, 2 and 3. Further, assume that the context distribution follows Assumption 4, following the Batched-ETC algorithm, the player-optimal stable regret for $p_i \in \gN$ is $Reg_i(T) = \gO (\frac{\log T}{\tilde{\lambda}^2 \Delta_{\min}^2} + \frac{\log T}{\Delta_{\min}^2})$.

results.notes: Proof also has additive 6NK log_2(4 sqrt2 Delta_1/Delta_min) term absorbed. Batched-ETC requires fewer inputs than BARB but shares setting s1.

conditions: Assumption 5: CDF of delta_min satisfies F(Delta) <= c Delta for Delta <= Delta_0

source.label: thm:asymptotic_upper_bound
source.quote: Under Assumption 5, when $T$ is sufficiently large, the regret of the BARB algorithm satisfies $Reg_i(T) = \tilde{\gO}(T^{2/3})$, $\forall i \in [N]$.

results.notes: Obtained from Theorem 3.1 since Delta_min >= (log T/(cT))^{1/3}. Instance-independent given the regularity constant c.

symbols.f_c: constant depending only on the CDF-regularity constant c

conditions: instance satisfies Assumption 5 uniformly over T (c = 3, Delta_0 = 1/16)
context distribution may depend on T
holds for at least one player i (not a fixed player)

source.label: thm:asymptotic_lower_bound
source.quote: Let $N = K = 3$. For any policy $\pi$, there exists an instance satisfying Assumption 5 such that for some constants $c,\Delta_0 > 0$, when $\Delta \leq \Delta_0$, the CDF of $\delta_{\min}$ obeys $F_T(\Delta) \leq c \Delta$ for all $T\ge1$. Then at least one player suffers regret $\Omega(T^{2/3})$, i.e., there exists $i \in [N]$ such that $Reg_i(T) \geq f(c) T^{2/3}$, where $f(c)$ depends only on $c$.

results.notes: Proof by contradiction via two-instance change of measure; d = 4 in construction. Max-over-players regret lower bound.

symbols.Delta_alg: gap threshold Delta defining the regret benchmark and given as algorithm input

conditions: access to an (alpha, gamma, eps)-approximation oracle
regret is the alpha-approximate Delta-optimal stable regret
tuning: eta = R sqrt(d log((1+T B_x^2/lambda)/delta)) + lambda^{1/2} B_theta, delta = 1/T

source.label: thm:adversarial_context_upper_bound
source.quote: Following the AdECO algorithm with parameter $\Delta$ and $\varepsilon$, the $\alpha$-approximate $\Delta$-optimal stable regret for $p_i \in \gN$ is $Reg_i^{\alpha, \Delta}(T) = \gO (\frac{Nd \log^2 T}{(\Delta - \varepsilon)^2} + \frac{\Delta + \varepsilon}{2} \cdot T)$. $\Delta$ is an algorithmic input, and the above regret bound holds uniformly for any choice of $\Delta$.

results.notes: Quantity mapped to alpha_regret, though benchmark mixes exact and alpha-approximate stable shares. Bound independent of alpha (Remark 4.1).

source.label: thm:adversarial_context_upper_bound
source.quote: By setting $\Delta = \gO(T^{-1/3})$, $\varepsilon = \Delta / 2$, we have the regret upper bound as $\gO(T^{2/3})$.

results.notes: Hides N d log^2 T factors; the benchmark itself depends on the chosen Delta.
